html:
Sobhuza II was king of Swaziland from 1899, when he was a baby, until his death in 1982, one of the longest reigns on record.

Under British rule he fought to recover the land lost through the concessions, raising money from his people to buy it back. He led Swaziland to independence from Britain on 6 September 1968 as a constitutional monarchy.

In 1973 he scrapped the constitution, banned political parties and ruled by decree, setting up a system of local councils loyal to the crown. He revived ceremonies such as the reed dance and Incwala. His heir, Mswati III, still rules as an absolute monarch in Eswatini.
